deep_dive.title: Turn-Based Combat Arena: A New Framework for Multiagent Training and Game Balancing
deep_dive.abstract: This paper is the first in a series on Turn-Based Combat Arena, a configurable framework for turn-based strategy games designed to support the efficient training and evaluation of machine learning agents. The proposed framework enables flexible modification of game rules and parameters, allowing rapid experimentation across diverse scenarios. Its architecture is optimized for high-throughput simulation, supporting tens of thousands of games per second and enabling the storage and processing of billions of gameplay records on a single machine. The problem of balancing the game, and particularly the parameters of game units, is investigated in detail. We evaluate several optimization approaches and show that multiple methods converge to comparable solutions, suggesting robustness in identifying balanced game configurations. These results indicate that the framework can serve as a practical platform for both game design analysis and agent training.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Introduces Turn-Based Combat Arena, a configurable high-throughput multiagent simulation framework for turn-based strategy games, enabling efficient training and evaluation of learning agents and supporting game-balancing optimization.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 多智能体游戏研究需要高吞吐、可配置的训练与评估环境，而现有平台较难兼顾灵活调整和超大规模数据管理。本文提出回合制战斗竞技场框架，支持快速修改规则与游戏参数，单机每秒可模拟数万局并存储处理数十亿条对局记录。文中以单位参数平衡为任务评估多种优化方法，结果表明多类方法能够收敛。该框架为多智能体强化学习提供算法训练、对比和游戏平衡研究的规模化平台，具有较强的基础设施价值。
